column2: req_desc

Keyboard-built layout
A designer who signs up through the UI builds a named area on a Blank layout with only the keyboard. The layout, with its canonical CSS and HTML, is stored and still listed in their library after a reload.

Accounts and sessions
Sign-up, sign-in and sign-out follow the username and password rules and answer with the statuses, bodies and messages published in API and Business rules, carrying the session in the mullion_session cookie.

Layout library
The library lists every layout the designer owns or has joined, newest first, and keeps them after a reload and a server restart. The New layout dialog checks the layout name and the starter template.

Grid keyboard and dialogs
The grid cells are one Tab stop whose arrow, Shift+arrow, Enter, Delete, Backspace and track keys work as published. Every dialog keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Undo and redo
Control+Z and Control+Shift+Z (Command on macOS) undo and redo the designer's own last change as new changes, with the published announcements, from any editor control except a text field.

Track sizing journey
The founder types sizes into the column and row size fields and sees the grid, the preview, the resolved widths and the generated CSS change in place. Refused sizes leave the layout as it was, confirmed through the API.

Track size forms
Every published track size form is accepted and stored, shown and generated in its canonical form.

Track size refusals
A track size that fails a check is refused with the message of the first failing check, in the published order, as a 422 from the API and in the Edit problem alert, and the field keeps the old size.

Resolved widths
Each column header's resolved-width readout equals that column's computed width in the live preview at the current preview width, rounded half up.

Painted area journey
The founder drags across cells to name an area, extends it by dragging an adjacent rectangle with the same name, and renames it. The result shows in every surface and in the stored layout.

Grid and area block markup
The editor grid publishes its cells, headers and area blocks with the roles, accessible names and data attributes given in Screens and layout.

Area rename everywhere
Renaming an area changes its name at once in every scope, in the grid, the preview, the generated HTML and CSS and every open editor and view of the layout. Saved versions keep the old name.

Canonical generated code
The Layout CSS and Layout HTML text and the API's css and html fields follow the generation rules byte for byte.

Area rules journey
A designer working by keyboard selection meets the name, overlap and shape refusals with the dialog left open, and clears cells. The stored layout changes only for accepted edits.

Area names
Area names follow the published name rule and the reserved name, with their exact messages.

Overlap and shape refusals
An area save that would overlap another area or leave an area that is not one rectangle is refused with the exact message, and nothing changes.

Clearing cells
Delete or Backspace empties the selected cells and removes any area left with no cells, unless the clear would leave an area that is not one rectangle, as qualified in Business rules.

Track add and remove journey
By grid keys and by buttons, the founder adds columns and rows inside areas and removes tracks that areas use. The stored layout matches the published rule.

Adding tracks inside areas
A new column or row joins an area wherever that area spans both neighbouring tracks, and every other new cell is empty.

Removing tracks
Removing a column or row removes those cells from every area, removes any area left with no cells, and announces each removed area.

Track count and gap limits
Track counts stay from 1 to MAX_TRACKS and gaps stay whole pixels from 0 to 200, each refusal with its exact message.

CSS round trip journey
The founder edits Layout CSS, applies it with the button or Control+Enter, fixes a line error, and sees the grid, the preview and the stored layout follow the CSS.

Accepted CSS
Apply CSS accepts the published rules, properties, whitespace and comments, and treats the CSS as the whole layout.

CSS errors by line
CSS with an error is refused with only the first error by line, in the exact published copy, while the typed text and the layout stay as they were.

Areas matched by name
Applied CSS keeps areas whose names already exist, reports added and removed areas by name, and CSS whose result equals the current layout creates no revision.

Breakpoint journey
The founder adds a breakpoint, rearranges its areas, sets its own gap, and steps the preview width across it in both directions. The stored layout and the generated media block follow.

Breakpoint limits and inheritance
Breakpoints follow the published width range, uniqueness and count limit. Each starts with its own copy of the grid in effect just below it and inherits its gap until set.

Breakpoint CSS
Each breakpoint renders as one exact media block, including its gap only when it has its own and the published display rules for areas it hides or shows.

Preview width and scope in effect
The Preview width slider resizes the preview by pointer and by the published keys. The tab in effect and its announcement follow the width, and selecting a tab moves the width.

Breakpoint Fold glide
When the scope in effect changes, each area block present before and after glides from its old cells to its new cells within the published time, and new blocks appear at once.

Track resize journey
The founder resizes columns and rows with the separators by keyboard, mouse and finger. The stored sizes match the steps taken.

Separator keys
Separator arrow keys change a track by one unit step within its range, aria-valuetext shows the canonical size, and separators of auto and minmax tracks are disabled.

Separator drag
Dragging a separator by mouse, pen or finger changes the track one step per whole 20 pixels of travel, shows the size during the drag, and sends one change on release.

Co-editing journey
Two designers in one layout see each other in Designers here and see each other's changes live. When both change one column at the same moment, the first arrival wins and the other sees the conflict notice.

Presence
Designers here lists every designer with the layout open, backed by an expiring Valkey presence key, and drops a designer as qualified in Business rules.

Live delivery
Every applied change shows in every other open editor and view page of the layout within 2 seconds, without reload, with the published announcement.

Server order and conflicts
Changes apply in server arrival order with revisions counting up by one. A stale change that touches a target another designer changed since its base revision is refused with 409 and never dropped silently.

Editor notices
Conflict and restore notices slide in at the top of the editor, stay 8 seconds, slide away, and can be dismissed early.

Version restore journey
The founder saves versions, compares them in the drawer, and restores one while the guest designer edits. Both editors and the API show the restored layout and the new version.

Saving versions and the drawer
Save version stores the whole layout as the next numbered version without changing the revision, and the Versions drawer lists versions oldest first and slides in and out within the published time.

Version differences
Compare lists the differences between two versions in the exact published order and wording.

Exact restore
Restoring a version brings back its tracks, gaps, areas and every breakpoint exactly, as one new revision and one new version. History is never rewritten, and older collaborator changes are refused as conflicts.

Developer view journey
A signed-out developer opens the view link, steps the preview width, reads the exact code, and sees the founder's change live. After the link is regenerated or revoked, the old link shows the not-available page.

Read-only view
The view page renders no editing control, its keys change nothing, and no request made through a view link can change the layout.

Link lifecycle
View links move from none to active to revoked or replaced, and co-edit links can be regenerated. Each change takes effect on the very next request, and the co-edit link adds the visitor as a collaborator whom the owner can remove.

Not found and request limits
The API follows the single published error order, answers 404 and never 403 for anything a visitor cannot open, refuses oversize bodies with 413, and never serves source files or credentials.

Phone editing journey
At 375 by 812 the founder switches editor panes, taps to place the cursor, and drags a finger across cells to name an area. The stored layout gains that area.

Editor widths
The editor uses three panes at 1280 by 800, two columns at 768 by 1024 and the Editor panes tabs at 375 by 812, with no horizontal page overflow and touch targets of at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Starter templates
A layout created from Blank, Holy Grail, Dashboard Shell or Magazine Spread holds exactly that template's published tracks, gaps, areas, breakpoints and code and nothing else, and the shipped app starts with no designers and no layouts.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion on, the drawer slide, the notice slide and the Breakpoint Fold glide happen at once, with the same end state and announcements.

Drafting-table look
The editor reads as a drafting table: a warm off-white page, blueprint-blue hairline gridlines on every canvas, heavy sans headings, monospace equal-width numerals for every track value, a burnt-orange accent and no gradients.

Valkey outage journey
On the copy whose Valkey is unreachable, the founder opens and edits a layout. Changes save and survive a reload, while the paused notice shows and another open editor stays unchanged until it reloads.

Health and live flag
/api/health and the layout's live field report whether Valkey answers, and the editor shows the live-paused notice as soon as it loads when live is false.

Saving without live delivery
With Valkey unreachable, changes, versions and links still save through Postgres, nothing is pushed live, and Designers here lists only the designer themself.

Grading setup route
POST /api/grading/setup with the right key creates the published users, layouts, versions, collaborators and links in one call. With any other key it looks absent.

Configuration from the environment
Every service URL, credential, limit and the grading key are read from the published environment variables at start, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with exactly the string keys _schema (run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app names every shipped package and its licence. Shipped packages are the production dependency tree, npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres and Valkey. It uses no other database, file-based store or extra service.
The app loads no font, script, stylesheet or image from another origin.
The provided service configuration and dev compose files are left unchanged.
Server and client source is written in TypeScript.
